PUBLIC INFORMATION

Mayor Pro Tempore / District 1 Councilmember Jawane Hilton will be participating at
a remote teleconference location as follows: San Antonio Marriott Rivercenter on the
River Walk, 101 Bowie Street, San Antonio, TX 78205 (precise location to be
determined; inquire with front desk). Mayor Lula Davis-Holmes and Councilmembers
Dear, Hicks, and Rojas will be participating in the City Council Chambers.
The remote teleconference location is accessible to the public to provide public
comment from that location using the teleconference instructions noted below. A
copy of the agenda will be posted at the remote teleconference location.

To participate via remote teleconference, members of the public can call
1-669-900-6833 (Meeting ID: 8 437 662 1373) on the date of the meeting during the
portion of the agenda entitled “Oral Communications” to provide public comments.

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the
jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council
during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral
Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the
agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the
Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of
one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally
3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Presentation made by Assistant City Attorney Ben Jones, Saied Nasseh, the consultant who drafted the zoning code Vivian, and members of the community development department staff. 
Mayor Pro-Tem expressed concern about the fast food places with drive-thrus coming to communities as the residents have expressed not wanting anymore drive thru restaurants. MPT is proposing drive thru restaurants within 100 feet of residents be prohibited. He would like that worked into the zone somehow some way. 
Saied stated Assistant City Attorney Ben Jones could possibly work that language in. Mayor Davis-Holmes stated that she also wanted to add language about liquor stores, car wash businesses, gas stations, as well as auto repair shops. 

Mayor asked to hear from the rest of council to chime in as well. MPT stated that we have to put a limit on these types of businesses. He also stated that the liquor stores are also price gauging. 

Councilman Dear asked if the existing businesses in these categories would be exempt from these restrictions. Said shared that is up to council but it is intended to be for new businesses. 
Ben Jones stated that change of ownership does not change or implement the change for existing businesses. He also stated that he will draft some language to reflect the recommendations from council as has been suggested tonight. 
Mr. Jones explained verbally the changes he would make for each section of the code related to the recommendations that council suggested. There are several places for notations to be added regarding the CMX zones and the 100 feet recommendation as stated by MPT Hilton. 
Mayor asked for consensus on all recommendations and there was a unanimous consensus. 
The mayor asked about the items that are mandated by state and Saied stated that there are rules around emergency housing regulations, transitional supportive housing and others are the ones that the state is mandating we put in residential areas. Councilman Hicks shared that he has received several calls from residents about some of the state mandates that are impacting our neighborhoods specifically relates to population density. 
The mayor wanted to point out the difference between what council controls and what is coming from the state as a mandate.
